pandas: A library for handling table data (like Excel)
pd: Uses pandas under the short name pd (import pandas as pd)
Series: One column of pandas data (a named 1-D array)
read_csv: Reads a CSV file into a DataFrame
to_csv: Writes a DataFrame to a CSV file. index=False leaves out the row numbers
to_csv.index: False leaves out the row numbers
loc: Selects rows and columns by name (label). df.loc[row, column]
iloc: Selects rows and columns by number. df.iloc[0, 1]
values: The list of a dictionary's values. In pandas, takes out the contents as a NumPy array
head: The first few rows
sort_values: Sorts by value. ascending=False sorts largest first
sort_values.ascending: True sorts smallest first, False largest first
groupby: Splits into groups by a column's values. Then summarize with mean() and so on
agg: Does several summaries (mean, total and so on) per group at once
query: Selects rows with a condition string. df.query("milk > 30")
isin: Whether a value equals any item in a list
apply: Applies a function to each row or column
rename: Changes column or row names. rename(columns={"old": "new"})
dropna: Removes rows with missing values. subset= chooses the columns to check
dropna.subset: Limits the columns checked for missing values
fillna: Fills missing values with a chosen value
merge: Joins two tables side by side on a shared column (SQL JOIN). on=, how=
merge.how: How to join. "inner" (in both), "left" (keep all of the left) and so on
concat: Joins tables by stacking them (or side by side)
crosstab: A table counting each combination of two columns (a cross-tabulation)
to_datetime: Turns strings into dates and times
dt: The way into the year, month, day and so on of a date column (df["date"].dt.month)
days: The number of days in a length of time
get_dummies: Splits a category column into columns of 0 and 1 (one-hot)
cut: Divides numbers into ranges and makes them categories
